title: Pinned version interface spec and regression harness for model onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a machine-readable interface stability specification and an automated regression harness that together form the gated contract for pinning a model version into the Redwood catalog. The spec must cover: prompt/role/chat shapes, parameter semantics (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, streaming flags), output envelope fields (choices, reasons, metadata), and performance profile metrics that we publish alongside a pinned version. The regression harness will validate semantic and performance stability against a golden snapshot before a pin can be released.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable spec (YAML+schema) exists that defines required stable fields for pinned versions: prompt format, stable parameter names, response envelope, and required metadata keys.
The spec is integrated into model-onboarding CI: any pin attempt must pass the regression harness before the 'pinned' state is allowed in the catalog.

Regression harness runs a) functional checks (golden prompts -> pass/fail with configurable tolerance), b) performance checks (p50/p95/throughput thresholds), and c) parameter passthrough tests (ensure user params are honored or appropriate fallback used).
Documentation and onboarding checklist updated (console UI docs + onboarding PRD linked) and a public-facing model catalog page shows a signed-off performance profile for each pinned version.
No breaking changes to parameter names/defaults or to the canonical output keys are permitted without a major-version pin and explicit migration notes. CI gates this validation.
Security review completed for any step that exposes internal metadata or runtime identifiers in the public catalog.
implementation_notes: Represent the contract as a single YAML schema plus a generated JSON-LD manifest included with every pinned model artifact.
Add a lightweight verifier service in onboarding CI that loads the manifest, runs the harness against a staging runtime, and emits a signed attestation artifact if all checks pass.
Parameter compatibility rules: renames are breaking; new optional parameters are allowed if defaults maintain previous behavior; default value changes require explicit opt-in and a migration pin.
Output envelope stability: 'choices[].text' and 'choices[].index' are stable; engine-internal fields may be namespaced under 'internal.*' and are not guaranteed stable unless explicitly listed.
Tokenization/encoding: include tokenizer checksum and vocabulary version in the manifest. Variations in tokenizer MUST be considered breaking unless an explicit compatibility shim is published.

Performance profile format: include standardized buckets (seq_len: 32/64/128/256/512/1024), p50/p95 latency for single-request and batched throughput for 1/4/8/16 request batching sizes, and memory usage estimates on the reference hardware build.
We will store golden outputs as compressed fixtures in the onboarding-artifacts S3 prefix; harness should support a 'regenerate' mode for maintainers with an audit log.
test_plan: Functional regression suite: 250 representative prompts across completion, chat, and structured-output use cases. Each prompt has a tolerance rule: exact-match for structured outputs, BLEU/ROUGE thresholds for deterministic tasks, and embedding-similarity thresholds for paraphrase-tolerant checks.
Parameter passthrough tests: systematically vary temperature/top_p/stop/stream to confirm runtime honors values and that fallback policies are applied only when documented.

Performance checks: run latency microbenchmarks on the canonical staging hardware (gpu-a100-40gb-v2) for the standard seq_len buckets. Gate fails if p95 latency increases >10% relative to the golden profile or throughput drops >15%.
Stress/regression: run 1-hour soak at target qps for Dedicated-like config to catch memory leaks or KV cache regressions.
Security smoke: ensure no sensitive internal runtime tokens or KMS identifiers are leaked into the published manifest or catalog page.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge YAML schema + verifier service into onboarding pipeline behind feature flag.
Step 2: Run verifier against 5 recently onboarded models in staging to calibrate thresholds and surface false positives.
Step 3: Require attestation for any new pinned model; legacy pinned models get a 6-week grace window to opt-in to manifest generation.
Step 4: After 4 weeks of stable runs, flip the feature flag to make attestations blocking for pin transitions in prod catalog.
Step 5: Monitor pinned-model rollouts for 30 days with SLO/alerting on catalog availability and pinned rollback rate.
open_questions: What exact numeric thresholds should be default for NLP-style generation tolerances vs structured-output strictness? (PM/Alex to decide)
How do we present 'recommended quantization variant' in the public profile without exposing internal perf tuning details? (Security/Product trade-off)
Should renaming of output envelope keys ever be allowed under a compatibility shim if we also provide a translation layer in the runtime?
What is the supported policy for minor tokenizer fixes that do not materially change tokenization distribution?
